description: The workspace webview shows the ship-served lattice client (any user-configured URL, so the pattern is any host), so everything here is reachable by whatever the ship serves and each grant is justified on that basis. pick_upload, save_vault and pick_vault all open a native dialog and act ONLY on what the user then picks: a hostile page gets nothing without a visible OS dialog and a deliberate choice in it. open_external_url sends target=_blank links (the clearweb share link) to the system browser, refusing anything outside http, https, mailto and tel, enforced in rust rather than in the page. backup_write takes bytes for an EXISTING schedule id only; the page cannot choose the directory or the filename, both come from the stored schedule, and the schedule's own retention bounds how many files it can leave behind. NOTE: save_vault and pick_vault were missing here until the scheduled-backup work, which meant vault export and restore in the desktop app failed on 'not allowed. Command not found' — deny-by-default is right, but a command the client calls and never gets is a feature that silently does not exist.
